key_claim_C2_water_neutrals_reproduced_j: In water the neutral-solute spreads are 0.096 (H2O) and 0.161 (acetamide) kcal/mol, i.e., close to the ~0.1 kcal/mol claim with only a modest deviation for acetamide.
key_claim_C2_water_ions_reproduced_justi: In water the ion spreads are 1.21 (NO+) and 0.66 (CN−) kcal/mol, exceeding the ~0.5 kcal/mol bound stated in the paper.
key_claim_C3_toluene_COSMO_ion_pathology: In toluene COSMO deviates strongly for ions (NO+ and CN− are ~7–8 kcal/mol less stabilizing than C-PCM/IEF-PCM/SS(V)PE), reproducing the low-dielectric COSMO ion pathology described in Table 1/Sec. 2.4.
absolute_number_gap_root_cause: Different cavity construction (PySCF Bondi/vdW radii vs Chipman/Herbert isodensity ρ0=0.001 a.u.) shifts absolute electrostatic solvation energies substantially, especially for ions; additional smaller gaps may come from discretization/implementation details and exactly which COSMO scaling/renormalization is used in PySCF.
one_line: Cross-method agreement in water is reproduced for neutrals but not for ions, while the low-dielectric COSMO ion failure is clearly reproduced; absolute values differ largely due to cavity-model mismatch.
notes: This replication directly tests C2/C3-style cross-method consistency using four ASC-PCM variants available in PySCF, but does not test C1’s formal operator-equivalence claim and cannot fairly assess C4’s SVPE absolute numbers because the cavity definition is intentionally different; the paper’s 'even at eps_s=2' sub-claim is not cleanly tested here because the toluene runs show much larger spreads (and eps=2.4, not 2.0).
